cdp.name: CDP
cdp.gloss: Customer Data Platform — the unified store of who your customers are.

perso.name: Personalization (1:1)
perso.gloss: Tailoring the message to the individual, not the segment.

genai.name: Generative AI
genai.gloss: Models that produce content — copy, images, replies — from a prompt.

agentic.name: Agentic AI
agentic.gloss: Systems that don't just generate, they decide and act toward a goal.

decis.name: Agentic decisioning
decis.gloss: An agent choosing what to say, when, how often and on which channel — per person.

bandit.name: Bandits / RL
bandit.gloss: The maths that lets a system learn which choice wins by trying and measuring.

cep.name: CEP
cep.gloss: Customer Engagement Platform — where this messaging actually runs.

geo.name: GEO
geo.gloss: Generative Engine Optimization — being visible inside AI answers.

govern.name: Governance
govern.gloss: The controls that make automated decisions safe, explainable and legible.

stories.head: Domo Chief Design Officer on speed vs. trust in AI product design
stories.plain: Domo's design chief argues that moving fast with AI without first building user trust is the bigger risk — not moving too slowly. For MarTech buyers and builders, this reframes the usual 'ship fast' mantra: governance and trust need to be baked in from the start, not bolted on after launch.

stories.head: Treasure AI product team: why the CDP had to stop storing and start deciding
stories.plain: Treasure AI's product team explains their shift from a passive data store to an active decisioning layer inside their CDP. This matters because it signals a broader industry move: CDPs are evolving from data warehouses into systems that autonomously act on customer data, blurring the line between CDP and agentic decisioning platforms.

stories.head: IAB updates standard for disclosing AI in ads
stories.plain: The IAB has redrawn its AI disclosure rules, placing the line around anything that changes how consumers perceive authenticity, identity, or what is real. This is an industry standard update — not just guidance — so it directly affects how brands must label AI-generated creative, which changes buying and compliance processes across the ad ecosystem.

stories.head: AI visibility index shows which brands are disappearing from AI answers
stories.plain: Research reveals a growing gap: brands that rank well on Google can be nearly invisible inside AI-generated answers. Traditional search authority no longer predicts AI recall. This matters because AI answers are increasingly where B2B and B2C buying journeys start, forcing marketers to rethink what 'visibility' even means.

stories.head: HubSpot July 2026 updates: Agent Hub arrives, centralising all AI agents
stories.plain: HubSpot's July release introduces Agent Hub, a single console for managing every AI agent across the platform. This is a structural product change — not a logo deal — that signals how major CEPs are tackling the governance problem of running multiple autonomous agents, and sets a template other platforms will follow.

stories.head: How to stop overpaying for AI complexity: match the tool to the task
stories.plain: A practical framework for choosing between rule-based, predictive, generative, and agentic systems by comparing their costs and risks. The core argument — start with the lightest approach that can do the job — directly shapes how marketing teams should evaluate and budget AI purchases, countering vendor hype for heavier stacks.

stories.head: Treasure AI: CDP evolves from data store to decision engine
stories.plain: Treasure AI's product team explains why their CDP was rebuilt to stop storing and start deciding — shifting the platform from a passive data warehouse to an active decisioning layer. Four detailed conversations on roadmap and design give a rare inside view of how CDP architecture is changing to support real-time agentic marketing.

month.skicker: 30-day synthesis · the shape underneath the feed

themes.head: AI Search Visibility Is the New SEO Battle
body: Brands that spent years optimizing for Google are now discovering that AI-powered answer engines like Gemini and ChatGPT cite sources by entirely different rules. Multiple audits and index launches this month confirm that B2B brands in particular are going dark inside AI search results, losing discovery at the moment buyers are forming purchase intent.

The response from vendors is swift: free AI visibility checkers, manufacturer-specific audits, and structured citation research are all launching simultaneously. The strategic shift required is not a tweak to existing SEO — it means rethinking how brand information is structured, authoritative, and machine-readable at the generation layer, not the ranking layer.

themes.head: The Rise of AI Agents as Marketing Operators
body: AI agents are graduating from chatbot novelty to operational infrastructure. HubSpot's Agent Hub, Serval's Catalyst agent that builds automations autonomously, and Influ2's MCP for contact-level ABM all shipped this month — signalling that the agentic layer is becoming the new middleware of the marketing stack, not an add-on feature.

The decision that changes for marketers is not which AI tool to buy, but how to prepare brand assets, data schemas, and workflows so agents can act on them reliably. Getting brand-ready for agent discovery is now a prerequisite, not a future-proofing exercise.

themes.head: Scaling AI Wins Organizationally, Not Just Individually
body: The month's editorial pattern is striking: at least four pieces tackle why AI value stays trapped in pockets — individual experiments that never compound. The teams extracting the most from AI share a common trait: they treat AI adoption as a workflow and culture problem, not a tooling problem, with clear ownership and documented repeatable processes.

The practical implication is that leaders need to stop celebrating scattered wins and start engineering the conditions for replication. That means overcoming the three adoption barriers (skill gaps, trust deficits, and fragmented ownership) and converting proof-of-concept moments into organizational muscle memory.
ev: MarTech · Teams getting most from AI

themes.head: Trust & Transparency Becoming Hard Requirements
body: The IAB's updated AI disclosure standard for ads, combined with debates about personalization overreach and the speed-vs-trust tension in product design, point to a single convergent pressure: regulators, platforms, and consumers are all tightening the conditions under which AI-generated content and targeting are acceptable. Disclosure is shifting from optional best practice to enforceable norm.

For marketers, this raises the cost of corner-cutting: personalization that feels surveillance-like, or AI content that goes unlabelled, now carries measurable reputational and compliance risk. The design question is no longer just 'what can AI do?' but 'what must we tell people when it does?'
ev: Agile Brand · Speed vs. trust in design

themes.head: Trackingless Commerce Forces First-Party AI Platforms
body: With third-party ad tracking in structural collapse, this month's most telling signal is a top shopping app building its own AI marketing platform from scratch on first-party data. The old measurement infrastructure — pixels, cross-site cookies, deterministic IDs — can no longer be assumed, and brands relying on it are flying blind heading into the holiday season.

Inflation-squeezed consumers comparison-shopping harder than ever (96% actively hunting value) makes this crisis more acute: the brands that can accurately measure & attribute without third-party tracking will capture a disproportionate share of constrained holiday budgets. The implication is that investing in owned data pipelines and AI-native attribution is now a revenue-protection decision, not an infrastructure one.

month.takeaway: Every major signal this month points to the same underlying shift: AI is no longer a feature layer sitting on top of existing marketing infrastructure — it is becoming the infrastructure itself, which means visibility, trust, data ownership, and organizational readiness are now existential strategic bets, not optimization projects.
